rationale: Because Clarence Thomas is the most senior justice in the majority and his conference view offers the narrowest majority-capable rule (no provocation/bootstrapping; antecedent facts only insofar as they illuminate contemporaneous perception), he is most likely to assign and keep the opinion. The minority is likely to fracture over how strongly to reject the Fifth Circuit’s “snapshot” approach, increasing the odds of at least one separate dissent (and possibly a majority concurrence to emphasize administrability and Mendez limits).
